full_judgment: 4. On behalf of the pre-emptee-petitioner, the learned Counsel Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan submitted that the learned District Judge erred in law to set aside the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court. The learned District Judge misconceived that the pre-emptor-opposite-party is not a co-sharer in the suit case, as the holding and the Jama of the case land have been separated by the Mutation Case filed by the present pre-emptee- petitioner and a separate Khatian No. 76 has been prepared in his name. So, the learned Counsel submitted that the learned District Judge did not consider Exhibit Ka which is the separate Khatian prepared by the Mutation Case No. 717 of 1979-80. So, he submitted that pre-emptor-opposite-party is not a co-sharer in the case Jote. Further he submitted that subsequently when the pre-emptor-opposite- party found it difficult to cope with her claim, she claimed the case land by way of contiguous owner. But she did not implead all the contiguous owners of the case land and has not given any boundary of the same. So, the learned Counsel submitted that the trial Court considered all these things in detail and by his judgment and order dated 14-1-2003 disallowed the pre-emption case. The learned Counsel submitted that the learned District Judge without showing any reason in support of his decision set aside the judgment and order which bears no legal value. In this regard, the learned Counsel has relied in the case of Fatema Bibi vs Manik Lal Somaddar reported in 50 DLR (AD), 97 and submitted that the Hon'ble Appellate Division in that case filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act No. XXVIII of 1951) observed that since the Khatians are different, the pre-emptor cannot be held to be a co-sharer in the case holding and as such she is not entitled to pre-emption. The learned Counsel Mr Khan submitted that the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge is not sustainable in the eye of law.
